title: Surge in Mississippi: Democrat Scott Colom Slams D.C. Forecasters as He Grabs Shocking Senate Lead
snippet: As Democratic challenger Scott Colom takes an unexpected lead over Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi, he is calling out election handicappers for writing off the South.
content:
In one of the most stunning developments of the election cycle, Democratic candidate Scott Colom has taken a razor-thin lead over incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's U.S. Senate race. Latest returns from the Associated Press show Colom leading by roughly 2,500 votes, or under one percentage point. Should the lead hold, Colom would become Mississippi's first Black senator since the Reconstruction era and the state’s first elected Democratic senator since 1982.

Calling Out the 'Prognosticators'

With votes still being tallied, Colom isn't just celebrating his surprising performance—he's taking aim at the Washington insider class. On Monday, the Black district attorney publicly criticized election forecasters, specifically calling out The Cook Political Report for rating the race as "Solid Republican" throughout most of the campaign. Colom argues that such ratings create a self-fulfilling prophecy by stifling fundraising opportunities for Southern Democrats.

"At some point, we have to talk about @CookPolitical and other ‘prognosticators’ who had me and other southern candidates labeled as solid R for much of the campaign cycle," Colom posted on X. "They made it much more difficult to fundraise and are part of the reason the South has been neglected for so long."

Allegations of Bias Against Southern Races

Colom further alleged that when he directly challenged the race's rating, an analyst was "extremely condescending" toward him despite lacking local insight into Mississippi politics. He noted that this persistent beltway skepticism has repeatedly crippled Democratic campaigns across the region, pointing to candidates like Jaime Davis in Louisiana, who narrowly lost a Senate race that national Democrats largely ignored.

While The Cook Political Report did not immediately respond to requests for comment, the tight battle in Mississippi is already forcing a reevaluation of how national political experts assess races in the Deep South.
